title: GPU allocator safety checklist and IaC adapter guide
author: Maya Alvarez
body:
Overview:

This page is a combined safety checklist and Terraform/adapter guide for the GPU allocator components that schedule, reserve, and reclaim fractional and whole GPU capacity across production pools. It is written for infra engineers and SREs who own allocator logic, IaC modules, and the preflight gates used by CI/CD. The objective is to reduce production regressions from allocator changes and provide a deterministic rollback surface.

Scope:
- GPU allocator service (allocatord) and sidecars
- Warm-pool manager and preemptive seeding logic
- Tenant egress segmentation policies related to allocator decisions
- Terraform modules and the IaC adapter that exposes allocator knobs to teams

Owners and escalation:
- Primary owner: eng-infra - Allocator squad
- Secondary owner: eng-sre - Capacity squad
- Pager: allocator-oncall (rotation)
- Escalation path: oncall -> allocator tech lead -> infra manager -> platform engineer

Safety checklist (pre-merge):
1) Unit & integration tests:
   - All allocator code must have unit tests covering allocation heuristics for at least 95% of branches.
   - Integration tests must run against a small simulated pool (N=3) in CI that validates: placement, eviction, warm-pool seeding, and metric emissions.
2) IaC contract validation:
   - Terraform plans must be run with the IaC adapter in dry-run mode and diff reviewed.
   - Module interface cannot remove or rename stateful attributes without a compatibility shim.
3) Canaries and traffic shaping:
   - New allocator rollouts must use a 5% canary window for 24 hours before 25% rollout.
   - Canary nodes must be tagged with allocator-canary=true and isolated via egress fence.
4) Rollback rehearsals:
   - For any allocator binary change, run the rollback script against the staging warm-pool and validate state reconciliation within 10 minutes.
5) Observability and alarms:
   - Ensure the following metrics are present and green in Grafana before approval: allocator.success_rate, allocator.latency_p95, warmpool.fill_ratio, tenant_eviction_count.
   - Alert thresholds: allocator.success_rate < 99.5% over 5m; warmpool.fill_ratio < 30% for 10m; tenant_eviction_count > baseline + 50% in 15m.

Configuration table (minimum fields required in module):
| field | type | description | default |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| allocator.enabled | bool | Enable allocatord scheduling | true |
| warmpool.target_percent | number | Target warm-pool fill as percent of capacity | 20 |
| eviction.backoff_seconds | number | Backoff applied after eviction to same tenant | 300 |
| network.egress_segment | string | Egress segment id used by canaries | "egress-fence-main" |

Terraform adapter pattern (example):
- Design principle: modules must be additive and expose a single small map of knobs. Avoid exposing allocator internals.

Example module usage snippet (terraform):
```
module "allocator_profile" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@repo.redwood.com/infra/terraform//modules/allocator-profile"
  name   = "slo-balanced"
  knobs = {
    warmpool_target_percent = 25
    eviction_backoff        = 600
    preempt_mode            = "soft"
  }
  tags = ["team:search", "env:prod"]
}
```

CI/CD gates and checks:
1. Preflight: run tf plan with the "allocator-diff-checker" CI job which validates there are no unsupported state changes.
2. Integration: run e2e allocator simulation job (containerized) with test harness (see /infra/test-harnesss/allocator-sim).
3. Canary deploy: automated canary via deployment job that annotates canary nodes and waits for metric stabilization (p95 latency <= 120ms and eviction delta <= 10%).

Incident runbook (allocator regressions):
1) Detect: Pager triggers on allocator.success_rate or warmpool.fill_ratio.
2) Triage: Check recent deploys (gitops commit history) and Terraform plan diffs.
3) Immediate mitigation steps (ordered):
   a) Pause gitops reconciliation for allocator modules.
   b) Disable new allocation decisions by toggling allocator.enabled=false via feature flag (fast path).
   c) Scale the warm-pool by +30% using the warmpool_scaler endpoint: POST /api/v1/warmpool/scale {"delta_percent":30} (auth: allocator-admin).
   d) If tenant evictions spike, run redispatch: POST /api/v1/allocator/redispatch?mode=gentle and monitor for 5m.
4) Post-incident: create postmortem with timeline and include: commit hashes, tfplan artifacts, canary logs, metric graphs.

Testing matrix (minimal):
- Unit tests: fast, run on PR with every commit.
- Integration (sim): nightly and PR on large changes.
- Chaos run: weekly chaos job that simulates preemption and verifies allocator recovers within 3x baseline latency.
- Performance: monthly perf suite with N=100 nodes and mixed tenants.

Metrics and dashboards to maintain:
- allocator.success_rate (percentage)
- allocator.allocations_per_minute
- allocator.latency_p50/95/99
- warmpool.fill_ratio
- tenant_eviction_count (per-tenant)
- net.egress_bytes_by_segment

Appendix: useful commands and snippets
- Validate Terraform plan with adapter: 
  ./infra-tools/allocator-iac-adapter validate --plan=plan.tfout --profile=slo-balanced
- Rehearse rollback (staging): 
  ./scripts/allocator-rollback.sh --cluster=staging --timeout=600
- Quick metric check (prod): 
  curl -s "https://metrics-api.redwood.internal/series?name=allocator.success_rate&window=5m" | jq .

Related documents and background reading:
- Placement SLO-driven provisioning playbook (see related pages)
- Warm-pool sizing heuristics (arch notes)

Notes and rationale:
- We intentionally keep the IaC adapter surface minimal to avoid teams coupling to internal allocator heuristics. The warm-pool is the primary safety valve for short-term capacity perturbations, and the checklist emphasizes fast toggles and scale-up paths before aggressive evictions.

If you update this page, append a one-line summary, the date, and your name to the change log at the bottom of this page.
